verdicts.gap_description: The recurrence of Section 2 has a non-mex branch (`elif f(q-1,r) < q: f(q,r) = f(q-1,r)`); at (n,n) it would give d_n = d_{n-1} whenever d_{n-1} < n, and C0045's stated justification ('n>a gives f(a,n)=f(a,a)=d_a') establishes only the collapse of the first mex component, not that the mex branch applies at every (n,n). Consequently the step '|D_{<n} cap [1,d_n)| = n - delta_n' also silently assumes the d_a (a<n) are pairwise distinct (set cardinality equated with an index count), which is not among the premises listed under 'Also used'. So the identity rests on at least two unproved inputs beyond (P), contradicting 'rigorous conditional on one isolated game premise'. Both side conditions hold empirically (min(d_n - n) = 2 for n>=1 to n=20000) and are plausibly fillable, but they are absent from the proof.

verdicts.effectivity_check: No computable bound is produced anywhere. The only consequence asserted is the equivalence 'strip bound d_n = alpha*n + O(1) is equivalent to block count c_n = (sqrt(2)/2)*n + O(1) (given bounded delta_n)' — an equivalence between two unproved O(1) statements. No line produces any constant: the premise (P) is unproved (with the submission itself conceding the remaining step may be circular), and nothing in the submission can be evaluated for r = 1000 or any other input. The submission yields neither a bound nor a reassertion of existence with a bound; it fails the project's effectiveness goal outright.

Deeper issues, all fillable or dissolving: (i) premise (P) is invoked but never used in the counting (c_n is by definition truncated to [1,d_n)), so the identity is unconditional given the C0045 mex reduction -- the 'single input on trust' framing misdescribes the logical structure; (ii) the exactness of the mex reduction at every n needs branch (B) never to intercept the diagonal (d_{n-1} >= n), which C0045's stated justification (branch (A)) does not establish (verified to n=10,000); (iii) the corollary's equivalence requires delta_n = O(1), unproved (empirical max delta_n = 1 to n = 10,000) and per the submission's own C0049 analysis as hard as the strip bound.

verdicts.effectivity_check: No computable bound is produced; no line yields any constant or bound on N(r). The submission states the open content explicitly: 'The boundedness of delta_n and c_n's slope is the open content (= C0052 strip bound).' The corollary is a conditional reformulation: d_n = n + 1 - delta_n + c_n makes the strip bound equivalent to a block-count asymptotic only given bounded delta_n, which is unproved and (per the submission's own C0049 correction) equivalent to the hard overlap-density claim. The identity is exact and effective as a formula, but it reasserts the target in new variables rather than bounding it.
